# Phase 24: ranking by a float32 bound (negative result)

What is left of the tier's quality gap belongs to selection: at 6.25%,
[Phase 21](PHASE_21.md)'s sessions keep 70.0% of the full cache's doc answers even at turn 0, and NIAH
has lost prompts at small budgets since [Phase 3](PHASE_3.md). [Phase 16](PHASE_16.md) found one
candidate cause: in most (step, layer, head) cells the K-th and (K+1)-th Quest bounds are equal in
bf16, the dtype the runtime ranks in, so `topk`'s tie order picks the last blocks, not the bound.
This phase asks whether computing the bound in float32 keeps more of the document. Questions and a
decision rule were fixed in `configs/phase24.yaml` before any run.

## What was built

- `top_blocks(..., dtype=torch.float32)` casts the query and the block minima and maxima before the
  bound. Policy `quest_f32` is rung 5 with it. Nothing else changes: same metadata, same K, same
  gather order. The tier shares the function, so the result applies to rungs 6 to 8 as well. Tests:
  a pair of blocks whose bounds tie in bf16 is ordered correctly in float32; the default is unchanged.

## Question 1: NIAH

prompt. The full cache scores 88.9%.

| 25% | 45 | 74.4% | 74.4% | 1 / 2 | 1 | no measurable effect | 7 |
| 12.5% | 45 | 64.4% | 62.8% | 1 / 3 | 0.62 | no measurable effect | 10 |

## What this means

- The bf16 ties are real, but they are ties between blocks that matter about equally. Breaking them
  by a finer bound picks different blocks, not better ones. That agrees with Phase 16's other
  finding: the bound captures most of the attention mass the oracle does, and the mass it misses
  does not predict which answers are lost.
- So the remaining document loss at small budgets is not a precision artifact of the ranking. The
  candidates left are the bound itself (min/max over 64 tokens is loose; Phase 4's 16-token blocks
  kept more, at a speed cost) and the selection's per-step, per-head granularity. Neither was
  tested here.
- The default stays bf16. Float32 costs a cast of the metadata per step and buys nothing measured.

## What this phase does not show

- One model (1B), one context (32K), 45 prompts and 20 sessions: effects of a few prompts would not
  resolve. The verdict is "no measurable effect", not "no effect".
- Speed was not timed (quality kernel).
